chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Ziyād al-Khazzāz, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the woman experiencing istiḥāḍah: what should she do when she sees blood and when she sees yellowness, and how much salat (prayer) she should leave. He said: “The minimum of menstruation is three [days], and its maximum is ten, and she combines between the two prayers.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman in this legal context
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), whose performance or suspension is being asked about
key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two prayers that are combined
key_terms.الصُّفْرَةَ: yellowish discharge considered in determining legal status
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةٌ: the minimum number of days for ḥayḍ
key_terms.عَشَرَةٌ: the maximum number of days for ḥayḍ

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the minimum and maximum length of ḥayḍ and the prayer of a mustaḥāḍah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mustaḥāḍah and the limits of menstrual bleeding in relation to salat (prayer). It states that the minimum ḥayḍ is three days and the maximum is ten, and it instructs her to combine between two prayers.
